text:
anya: heads-up — CI canary showed multiple OOMs on the new runtime image (after merge of PR #4223). failing jobs: runtime-inference-canary-5 and runtime-loadtest-2048. stack shows allocation spike from kv cache compaction path.

maria: ugh. which commit did that PR touch?

kevin: bisected to commit abc1234 (merge of #4223) — it replaced LRU eviction heuristics with LFU-ish counting and added a background "segment compaction" job. running `git bisect` locally reproduced quickly.

rachel: infra note: autoscaler emitted multiple node OOM events around 11:06 UTC during the canary, we also saw eviction churn in /var/log/messages. infra-bot attached the pod logs to the failing job.

anya: paste of the failing log (truncated):
```
2025-11-02T11:05:32Z runtime: kv_cache: start_compaction loop
2025-11-02T11:05:33Z runtime: alloc arena grow to 134MB
2025-11-02T11:05:33Z runtime: runtime: out of memory allocating 32MB for kv segment
panic: runtime: out of memory
```

kevin: quick profiling (pprof heap) from the reproduce run — top allocations are small kv segments and arena metadata. heatmap shows memory concentrated in many 16–64KB objects, and compaction attempts allocate temp buffers ~8–32MB which pushes worst-case over node memory on 4GB VMs. seems sequence-length sensitivity: longer sequences (>=2048) cause many more segment splits.

maria: this matches local repro with long-seq workload. Without compaction (flip flag `--kv-compaction-enabled=false`) the memory stays stable, though baseline memory is a bit higher long-term.

kevin: suspect regression is twofold: (1) the LFU counters keep per-segment metadata that doesn't amortize for short-lived keys, increasing fragmentation; (2) compaction does a copy-to-new-segment strategy that temporarily doubles peak memory. both are visible in flamegraphs.

rachel: CI perf job also flagged token throughput regression ~8% on the same build vs previous. might be related — extra compaction CPU cycles increase latency and reduce batching efficiency.

anya: action plan: 1) revert compaction change (candidate revert PR #4231) for canary, 2) add a safety patch to limit compaction memory growth (`--compaction-max-temp=16MB`), 3) run a focused bisect to separate LFU vs compaction effects. I'm opening a rollout-blocker label.

maria: please include a short reproducer script in the revert PR so QA can validate quickly. also add a feature flag gate for LFU replacement.

kevin: bisect notes I pushed to the issue: commits between def5678..abc1234 touched kv/eviction.go and scheduler/compactor.go. reproducer: `make repro-seq SEQ=2048 RPS=20 DURATION=60s` hits the OOM reliably on 4GB nodes.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy runtime-image:v2025.11.02-abc1234 -> FAILED (oom/killed) on cluster canary-2 at 2025-11-02T11:12:03Z.

anya: I'll open the revert PR and request emergency review from @maria and @kevin. tagging @rachel for any infra adjustments (temp bigger nodes for triage).

maria: thanks. once revert merges, let's run perf regression CI to confirm throughput restored and then iterate on a safer LFU+compaction design (prefer incremental in-place compaction, avoid peak doubling).

kevin: one more data point — turning off per-request KV cache prefetch reduced small-object churn in profiles. might be a complementary mitigation. adding to the issue.

rachel: noted. I'll standby to scale canary nodes to 8GB if needed for deeper profiling, but prefer revert first.

anya: creating PR now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4231 (revert compaction and reintroduce LRU flag). marking as rollout-blocker. :exclamation:

kevin: nice, adding perf unit tests that simulate long sequences and assert peak memory < 80% on 4GB. will post results in the issue.

maria: good work y'all. keep updates short here — once revert lands we'll coordinate the canary redeploy. :thumbsup:
